Review LiveKit?

Reviewers describe LiveKit in narrow but consistent terms: a reliable, open-source, modular base for real-time voice and WebRTC work. Users like that it plugs into many stacks, while several founders say they chose it for low latency, uptime, scalability, and the control to customize or self-host. Makers of Inworld, SpatialChat, and Talo by Palabra.ai offer little detail overall, but the strongest concrete feedback centers on deep integration, real-time audio pipelines, and handling complex infrastructure without giving up flexibility.

# The Best LiveKitAlternatives [...] 4.9 · 18 reviews

Learn more →

Daily leans into a batteries-included approach, making it attractive when you want to embed calling quickly without assembling a long list of surrounding services. Compared with LiveKit’s infrastructure-first posture, Daily more often feels like a complete platform for browser-based calls, with recording and live streaming capabilities that reduce how much you need to build and operate yourself.

It also stands out for offering a simple integration surface while still leaving room for lower-level control when you need a bespoke experience. That balance is useful for product teams that want to ship fast, but still expect to iterate on layouts, events, and real-time behaviors without fighting abstractions. [...] In evaluating LiveKit alternatives, the key considerations were integration speed and SDK ergonomics, reliability and latency under real-world load, scalability across geographies, and how much is included out of the box (recording/streaming, dashboards, plugins). We also weighed ecosystem fit for AI/voice-agent pipelines and telephony workflows, the end-user friction of joining sessions, and the quality of vendor support and iteration velocity—alongside practical pricing and operational overhead trade-offs.
